title: trailboss --json actions
description: `trailboss actions [--since 30m|2h|1d|ISO] [-n N]`: what Trailboss itself did, newest first (at most N, default 50): every agent it started, message it typed, merge, removal, stop, restore, delete and resume, on your command or by a documented trigger. Each is a line of a hash-chained record beside the index; `doctor` checks the chain.

seq.description: The action's number, from 1, counting up across the record's rotation.

at_ms.description: When it happened, in ms since the epoch.

at.description: The same time, as ISO 8601 in UTC.

kind.description: What Trailboss did: start (an agent in a new terminal), type (a message into an agent), merge (a task's branch, `task accept`), remove (a task's worktree and branch, or a queued task taken back), stop (a team or an until loop), restore (project files written back: `checkpoint restore`, `review --undo`), delete (a session's transcript), resume (a session restarted in its terminal). More may be added.

trigger.description: The command the action ran under: its subcommand words and the flags that change what it does, never a value you typed, e.g. `task add --yes`, `send --yes --queue`, `queue deliver`, `task start-due`, `until`, `resume --auto`.

via.description: For an action a background command took, the look that started it: `watch`, `events`, `serve` (a client following /events) or `send --yes --queue --wait`; null otherwise.

agent.description: The agent kind or definition it concerns, when known.

session.description: The session id it concerns, when known.

host.description: The host of the terminal it concerns.

terminal.description: The terminal's address in that host.

team.description: The team it was taken for: a team's lead start or a member started by its lead, or `team stop`.

outcome.description: ok, failed (Trailboss's own error in detail) or skipped (why in detail).

detail.description: Trailboss's own words: the error, why it was skipped, or a short note (what was merged into, how many files were written back). Never typed text, a brief, transcript content or a token.

prev.description: The SHA-256, as hex, of the line before this one in the record; 64 zeros for the first. `doctor` checks the chain.
